item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 7655ed9299035a88f31a7b52486b42833abbee23; a4848492c quotes the nine observed_on values in jt-60sa.yaml, adds _normalise_dates at edas.py:44 and applies it at edas.py:297, and adds test_real_facility_payload_serializes_observation_dates at tests/discovery/test_edas_scanner.py:82; 835784127 adds the route-counts fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's charge (plan §55 node 3) is to make the dates durable as strings, diagnose the exit 255 from full remote stderr and fix the cause with a test that serialises the real jt-60sa.yaml payload, and have a scoped scan persist the UDDB and LCDB route bindings; all four hold — jt-60sa.yaml:73 quotes the dates, edas.py:297 normalises before transport, tests/discovery/test_edas_scanner.py:82 loads the real config, and routes-after.json records UDDB 189 and LCDB 8,469 bindings where routes-before.json had none. The section-level done-when (signals leaving discovered) is the drain, deferred to the stage owner — see the first finding.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to unblock the EDAS scan blocked by two faults on the merged latter config: unquoted YAML dates that load as datetime.date and fail JSON serialisation in the remote payload, and a remote exit 255; the fix quotes the config dates and adds _normalise_dates (edas.py:44) applied at edas.py:297, and the exit 255 is diagnosed as the ssh-config sandbox fault worked around with the wrapper.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits [a4848492c, 835784127], the tests line names both the focused scanner gate and the scoped scan, after_suite records failure_count 0 for the focused file, and baseline_suite is left empty at manifest.md:21.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares imas_codex/config/facilities/jt-60sa.yaml, imas_codex/discovery/signals/scanners/edas.py, tests/discovery/test_edas_scanner.py and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/edas-scan-repair.html; git diff --stat 7655ed9..835784127 touches exactly those four files.

justifications.durability: test_real_facility_payload_serializes_observation_dates loads the real jt-60sa.yaml (nine routes, all str) and drives EDASScanner().scan through a patched remote that json.dumps the payload, so restoring an unquoted date fails it (confirmed independently, EXIT=1); _normalise_dates recurses through dicts and lists, so a date anywhere in the nested config is covered, not only observed_on.
justifications.evidence: I re-ran the focused scanner gate at 835784127 and got 32 passed with EXIT=0, matching after_suite; the reproduction pair is date-test-baseline.log (base 7655ed9, the real-config payload test fails, EXIT=1) and date-test-after.log (working tree) — and I independently confirmed the guard's sensitivity by unquoting one observed_on in a scratch copy, which flips the type from str to date and fails tests/discovery/test_edas_scanner.py:85. baseline_suite is empty so no suite-regression arm was measured, and the original exit-255 cause is inferred rather than proven.
justifications.fit: the commits a4848492c and 835784127 use conventional fix(signals)/docs(discovery) subjects with bodies and carry no plan or section label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: edas.py:297 normalises the config before the remote payload and jt-60sa.yaml quotes the nine observed_on values, matching the node's stated fix; the scoped scan then wrote UDDB and LCDB bindings (routes-after.json) where the graph had only EDDB before. The section-level drain was not performed, but the node declares that as the stage owner's.
justifications.reuse: a search over imas_codex for a date-normalisation helper found no existing general utility (only scattered .isoformat() call sites), so _normalise_dates is the first owner of that capability in the scanner; it is a private module helper, not a duplicated framework.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 7655ed9299035a88f31a7b52486b42833abbee23..835784127d1f7c45745ae5918f03180503f07446 lists only jt-60sa.yaml, edas.py, tests/discovery/test_edas_scanner.py and the fragment, all inside the declared write paths.
